title: Identifiability of wearer through sensor telemetry
description: Continuous collection of GPS position, timestamps, and activity data (heart rate, step counts) can uniquely identify the wearer's identity, location patterns, and health status, enabling profiling and tracking of the individual.
assumptions: The wearable device transmits identifiable sensor data that can be correlated with the wearer's identity.

title: Linkability of sensor data across systems
description: Sensor telemetry data (GPS, timestamps, health metrics) collected by the wearable device can be linked to other data sources (e.g., social media, other apps, health records), creating comprehensive user profiles and enabling cross-system tracking.
assumptions: The wearable device or its backend may share data with third-party services or other systems.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of sensitive health and location data
description: Heart rate, step counts, GPS position, and timestamps are sensitive personal data that could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through data breaches, insecure transmission, or improper access controls.
assumptions: The wearable device or its communication channel may lack adequate security controls.

title: Tampering with sensor telemetry data
description: Sensor data (heart rate, GPS, timestamps) could be altered, manipulated, or falsified by attackers, potentially leading to incorrect health assessments, insurance fraud, or misleading location tracking.
assumptions: The wearable device or its data pipeline may be vulnerable to data manipulation attacks.

title: Usurpation of wearer's data by unauthorized actors
description: Unauthorized actors could gain access to the wearer's sensor data and use it for impersonation, identity theft, or other malicious purposes without the wearer's consent.
assumptions: The wearable device or its backend may have insufficient authentication and authorization mechanisms.

title: Explicit Data Disclosure of Sensitive Sensor Data
description: Wearable device (P1) explicitly transfers personal data (GPS traces, device ID, timestamps, exercise sessions) to companion app (P2). This disclosure is by design but raises questions about data minimality - is all this data necessary for the app's functionality?
assumptions: The wearable device and companion app are part of the same system ecosystem, but data transfer still crosses a logical boundary.

title: Linkability of GPS Traces to Individual Identity

assumptions: GPS data contains location information that can be correlated with identity through device ID or other metadata.
uncertainty_note: Tree node L.1.1 is inferred; exact LINDDUN Pro node may vary.

title: Explicit Location Data Disclosure to Store
description: The Companion Mobile App explicitly transfers GPS location traces with timestamps to the Location History Store by design. This represents an intentional data disclosure where personal location data is transferred across a system boundary.
assumptions: The app is designed to write location data to the store as part of its functionality.

title: Location Data Linkability to Individual Identity
description: GPS location traces with timestamps can be linked to specific individuals, enabling reconstruction of movement patterns and association with other data sources to identify users.
assumptions: Location data contains sufficient granularity to be linked to individual users through device identifiers or user accounts.

assumptions: Location data is stored in a manner that preserves individual-level granularity rather than being aggregated or anonymized.

assumptions: The Location History Store may not have adequate integrity controls to prevent unauthorized modification of stored location data.
